title: Enabling 13K-Atom Excited-State GW Calculations via Low-Rank Approximations and HPC on the New Sunway Supercomputer
problem: GW approximation for excited-state calculations has prohibitive O(N^4) computational cost and O(N^3) memory usage, limiting simulations to approximately 2,700 atoms even on leadership supercomputers.
motivation: Accurate large-scale excited-state simulations enable practical design and discovery of next-generation semiconductor devices and materials.
method: Uses series of low-rank approximations to reduce GW from O(N^4) to cubic-scaling O(N^3) complexity and O(N^3) to quadratic O(N^2) memory usage. Implements massively parallel plane-wave GW with communication optimization strategies on Sunway supercomputer architecture. Efficient parallel data distribution and computation enable scaling across hundreds of thousands of cores.
key_novelty: Low-rank approximation framework reduces expensive GW calculations to cubic scaling, enabling mesoscopic-scale (13K+ atom) excited-state simulations.
contributions: Low-rank approximation technique reducing GW from O(N^4) to O(N^3) complexity and memory from O(N^3) to O(N^2)
Massively parallel implementation with 70x speedup via communication optimization on Sunway supercomputer
Demonstration of 13,824-atom excited-state calculations, 5x increase over prior 2,742-atom limit
Efficient scaling to 449,280 cores with execution time of minutes
baselines: prior GW implementations limited to 2,742 atoms
primary_theme: Low-rank GW approximations for large-scale excited-state calculations
